answer: A payout claim must wander a route before it counts: three relays drawn from the claimant's own address hash out of the established set, each stamping a nonce plus a small proof-of-work — basalt, slow to cut, instant to read. A stamp commits to the one claim it carried, so it cannot be reused, lent or pooled, and every head pays three relay fees per epoch. Two claims bearing the same stamp under the same nonce came from one hand. The summit is the tally: no three stamps, no share. A farm of N heads buys N routes it cannot share, and standing as a relay costs the very gate it dodges.
